content.text:
I submitted **index 1 (Sb fraction 0.195)** as the best composition. It gave the highest EQE I measured, **0.039%**. I used all 5 EQE measurements and 2 of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.150 | 0.023 |
| **1** | **0.195** | **0.039** |
| 5 | 0.367 | 0.015 |
| 14 | 0.502 | 0.008 |
| 23 | 0.680 | 0.007 |

- **Trend:** EQE rose steadily as the Sb fraction fell, then dropped at the most Pb-rich point (index 0). The peak is somewhere around Sb 0.2.
- **Structure:** index 1 and index 5 have nearly the same diffraction pattern. The closest match is a pyrochlore-type Pb₂Sb₂O₇ structure, with some possible lead-oxide (PbO₂-like) character. That match is only moderate (0.82 similarity at index 5).
- **Main uncertainty:** indices 2–4 (Sb 0.26–0.32) were never measured because the budget ran out. The trend suggests they are unlikely to beat index 1, but one of them could. In hindsight, the last measurement would have been better spent on index 2 or 3 than on index 0.
